title: Minimum Time to Remove All Cars Containing Illegal Goods
summary: Given a binary string representing train cars, where '1' indicates cars with illegal goods, determine the minimum time to remove all such cars using three operations: removing a car from the left end in 1 unit of time, removing a car from the right end in 1 unit of time, or removing a car from anywhere in 2 units of time.
statement: Given a binary string representing train cars, where '1' indicates cars with illegal goods, determine the minimum time to remove all such cars using three operations: removing a car from the left end in 1 unit of time, removing a car from the right end in 1 unit of time, or removing a car from anywhere in 2 units of time.
constraints: A 1 marks illegal goods and every such car must be removed.
Removing one car from either end costs one; removing an illegal car from anywhere costs two.
Return the minimum total time, while zero cars need no removal.
hints: Split the strategy into a processed prefix and a suffix removed from the right.
Track the cheapest way to clear all ones in the prefix: either extend it and pay two for a one, or remove the whole prefix from the left.
At each index update left=min(left+2*is_one,index+1), then combine it with the cost of deleting the unprocessed suffix.
Every solution has a final boundary: left DP optimizes everything before it and right-end removal handles everything after it; checking all boundaries is exhaustive.
editorial: Every solution has a final boundary: left DP optimizes everything before it and right-end removal handles everything after it; checking all boundaries is exhaustive.

tests.explanation: Remove a suitable prefix and suffix while paying two for any remaining internal one; the minimum total is 5.
Removing the single internal illegal car directly costs 2, which is cheaper than clearing an end to reach it.
